extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, trademark attorneys, and USPTO disciplinary/enrollment staff (practitioners subject to USPTO disciplinary rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO (suspension, probation, reinstatement, enforcement steps) when an attorney is disciplined by a state court. Covers notice, response rights, lengths of suspension/probation, OED enforcement powers, publication/notification, and examples of underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed by the USPTO Director when a practitioner has been suspended on ethical grounds by a state court (i.e., imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of California).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order (Complainant for Reciprocal Discipline) requests imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state court; the action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be mailed a Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice sent by certified mail; delivery date triggers 40-day response period. Failure to file a timely response is material to the determination of whether factual issues exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, it is appropriate to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly treats the respondent's non-response as justification for entering reciprocal discipline without further factual dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and form of discipline (suspension and probation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order suspension from practice before the USPTO for a specified period and impose a probationary period; in this case: suspension for two years and placement on two years' probation starting on the date the Final Order is entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies both suspension duration and concurrent/prospective probation, and may provide conditions for early reinstatement subject to regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is permitted to seek reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after serving thirty (30) days of the two-year suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reinstated under § 11.60, the respondent may be permitted to practice patent law before the USPTO during the probationary period unless the stay of suspension is lifted by order of the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice limitations during probation and § 11.14(a) condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If reinstated, the respondent may practice trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO during the two-year probationary period only if the respondent otherwise satisfies 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a) and unless the stay of the suspension is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order ties permission to practice certain matter types during probation to compliance with § 11.14(a) requirements (as a condition precedent) and to any USPTO Director orders lifting a stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's enforcement authority for probation noncompliance (Order to Show Cause process)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend the respondent for up to an additional twenty-three (23) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure set out: (a) OED issues Order to Show Cause; (b) send to respondent at last address of record pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); (c) grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond. After the 15-day response period, if OED remains of that opinion, OED may deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response, and argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension up to 23 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative to immediate enforcement: consideration during reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is not required to take immediate action described above if the respondent has not yet been reinstated; instead, the OED Director may consider purported failures to comply in connection with any request for reinstatement made by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED has discretion to defer issuance of an Order to Show Cause and treat alleged probationary noncompliance as a factor in reinstatement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and official notice of discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish notice in the Official Gazette and give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a model Notice of Suspension for publication and notes that disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room (with URL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for USPTO disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, specifically 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing statutory/regulatory authority frames the Director's power to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish/notify others of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of underlying attorney misconduct warranting suspension (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of the kind of misconduct that led to the state suspension: failing to file an Offer of Compromise with the IRS on behalf of clients; failing to perform legal services competently; failing to adequately communicate with clients; failing to provide a court-ordered accounting to a receiver; delaying approximately sixteen months before providing an accounting to opposing counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples illustrate factual bases that may support suspension on ethical grounds (competence, communication, failure to comply with court orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of disciplinary decisions for public reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a public access point for finalized disciplinary orders and supports transparency and notice to the bar and public.
